1.word_for_word: kṛṣṇaḥ nāthaḥ yeṣām — those whose protector is Kṛṣṇa; tebhyaḥ — for them
1.translation: The sense is ‘for those whose Lord and protector is Kṛṣṇa.’ The electronic source marks the corresponding verse text as uncertain here.

2.word_for_word: kruddhaḥ san indraḥ — Indra, having become angry; sāṃvartakam nāma — the group called Sāṃvartaka; saṃvartaḥ pralayaḥ — saṃvarta means cosmic dissolution; tat-kartāram meghānām gaṇam — the famous host of clouds that brings it about; prācodayat preṣayām āsa — he incited and sent them; kṛṣṇa-nāthānām ghāte katham pravṛttaḥ — how could he attack those whose Lord is Kṛṣṇa; ātma-sambhāvanayā nirasta-vivekatvāt — because self-conceit had destroyed his discrimination; īśa-mānī — thinking himself the lord; aham eva īśvaraḥ iti garvavān — proud with the thought ‘I alone am ruler’
2.translation: In anger, Indra sent forth the renowned host of Sāṃvartaka clouds. ‘Saṃvarta’ is the cosmic dissolution, and these are the clouds associated with producing it. How could Indra set out to destroy people whose protector is Kṛṣṇa? Because his self-importance had deprived him of discrimination. The following verses express this: he was ‘īśa-mānī,’ proud in the conviction ‘I alone am the lord.’

3.word_for_word: deva-helanam — disrespect toward a god; devasya mama avajñām — contempt for me, the god Indra
3.translation: ‘Disrespect toward the god’ means, in Indra's thought, contempt for himself.

4.word_for_word: adṛḍhaiḥ asamarthaiḥ — weak, incapable; karma-mayaiḥ — consisting of ritual actions; kriyā-nirvartyaiḥ — produced by rites; nāma-nau-nibhaiḥ — like boats that are boats only in name; ānvīkṣikīm — discriminative inquiry; ātma-anusmṛti-rūpām — consisting of recollection of the Self
4.translation: The supports on which the cowherds rely are, in Indra's contemptuous characterization, ‘unstable’ and ineffective because they consist merely of ritual acts—like vessels called ‘boats’ in name but incapable of carrying one across. ‘Ānvīkṣikī’ here means discriminative reflection in the form of recollection of the Self.

5.word_for_word: vācālam — talkative; bahu-bhāṣiṇam — speaking much; bāliśam — childish; śiśum — a child; paṇḍita-māninam — thinking himself learned; stabdham — proud, unbending; ajñam — ignorant; nindāyām yojitā api indrasyā bhāratī kṛṣṇam stauti — although Indra intends these as insults, his words can be read as praise of Kṛṣṇa; vācālam — source of scripture; bāliśam — childlike and free of ego; stabdham — bowing to none because none is above him; ajñam — ‘one from whom no knower is separate,’ hence omniscient; paṇḍita-māninam — highly honored by knowers of Brahman; kṛṣṇam — Kṛṣṇa, supreme Brahman of being and bliss; martyam — appearing human because of affection for devotees
5.translation: Indra's insults can, despite his intention, be understood as praise of Kṛṣṇa. ‘Talkative’ can point to him as the source of scripture; ‘childish’ to his childlike freedom from ego; ‘stiff’ to the fact that there is none superior before whom he must bow; ‘ignorant’ can be re-read as ‘one beyond whom there is no knower,’ hence omniscient; ‘thinking himself learned’ becomes ‘greatly honored by the knowers of Brahman.’ Kṛṣṇa is the supreme Brahman, the form of being and bliss, yet out of tenderness for his devotees he appears as a mortal human being.

6.word_for_word: avaliptānām — of the arrogant; mattānām — intoxicated; ādhmāyita-ātmanām — whose bodies or selves are swollen; dhunuta apanayata — shake off, remove; śrī-madena yaḥ stambhaḥ garvaḥ — the rigidity of pride produced by wealth and prosperity
6.translation: Indra orders the clouds to remove the swollen arrogance of those intoxicated by prosperity—to shake off the rigidity of pride produced by their fortune.

7.word_for_word: bibhyataḥ tān prati āha — he speaks to the clouds when they are afraid; aham ca iti — ‘I also’; anuvraje — I will follow immediately after you; marud-gaṇaiḥ deva-gaṇaiḥ saha — together with the hosts of winds or gods
7.translation: Seeing the clouds hesitate in fear, Indra reassures them: ‘I too will follow immediately, accompanied by the hosts of winds and other gods.’

8.word_for_word: maghavatā indreṇa nirmuktam bandhanam yeṣām — whose restraint was released by Indra; pralaya-abhiprāyeṇa baddhāḥ āsan — they had been held back for the time of dissolution; nirmukta-bandhanāḥ — now released; āsāraiḥ dhārā-sampātaiḥ — with torrents and sheets of rain; pīḍayām āsuḥ — they afflicted Vraja
8.translation: The Sāṃvartaka clouds had been held in reserve for the cosmic dissolution. Indra released that restraint, and once unleashed they afflicted Vraja with violent torrents and continuous sheets of rain.

9.word_for_word: stanayitnubhiḥ aśanibhiḥ — with thunderbolts; stanantaḥ garjantaḥ — thundering and roaring; marud-gaṇaiḥ āvaha-pravaha-ādi-vāyu-samūhaiḥ nunnāḥ — driven by the groups of winds such as Āvaha and Pravaha; jala-śarkarāḥ — hailstones, literally water-pebbles
9.translation: They thundered and hurled lightning, driven onward by the great groups of winds such as Āvaha and Pravaha. ‘Water-pebbles’ means hailstones.

10.word_for_word: sthūṇāvat sthūlāḥ — thick like pillars; abhreṣu muñcatsu satsū — while the clouds poured down; nata-unnatam nimnam unnatam ca — low and high ground; tad-viparītam yathā bhavati — becoming indistinguishable or reversed; bhūḥ na adṛśyata — the earth could no longer be seen
10.translation: The rain fell in pillar-thick streams. As the clouds continued pouring, low and high ground disappeared beneath the water until the surface of the earth could no longer be distinguished.

11.word_for_word: jāta-vepanāḥ — seized by trembling; jāta-kampāḥ — they began to shake

12.word_for_word: tatra paśūnām yānam viśinaṣṭi — he specifies the condition and movement of the animals; śira iti — by the verse beginning with ‘head’
12.translation: The verse beginning with the reference to their heads describes in particular how the animals were moving and protecting themselves in the storm.

13.word_for_word: gopa-gopīnām prārthanām āha — he gives the prayer of the cowherd men and women; tvam eva nāthaḥ yasya tat gokulam — the cowherd community whose Lord is you alone; gavām kulam vaṃśam — the herd and lineage of cows; naḥ asmān ca — and us; devāt indrāt trātum rakṣitum arhasi — you should protect from the god Indra
13.translation: The cowherd men and women pray: ‘Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa! You alone are the Lord of this Gokula. Protect the cows and us from the god Indra.’

14.word_for_word: vijñāpanāt pūrvam eva — even before they finished making their appeal; kupitena indreṇa kṛtam tat varṣam — the rain sent by the angry Indra; mene — Kṛṣṇa understood it to be so
14.translation: Even before their appeal was completed, Kṛṣṇa understood that this extraordinary rain had been produced by the angered Indra.

15.word_for_word: apartv iti — he explains how Kṛṣṇa knew; apagata ṛtuḥ yasya tat varṣam — rain occurring out of season; atiśayitaḥ vātaḥ yasmin — accompanied by excessive wind; śilā-mayam — full of hailstones
15.translation: Kṛṣṇa recognized it by its character: the rain was out of season, accompanied by extraordinary winds and filled with hail.

16.word_for_word: pratijñā-pūrvakam govardhana-uddharaṇam āha — he introduces the lifting of Govardhana with Kṛṣṇa's resolve; tatra pratividhim pratīkāram sva-sāmarthyena sādhayiṣyāmi — I shall provide the remedy by my own power; tena ca mauḍhyāt lokeśa-māninām — and by doing so, for those guardians of the worlds whose foolishness makes them proud; śrī-mada-lakṣaṇam tamaḥ hariṣyāmi — I shall remove the darkness characterized by pride in prosperity; bahu-vacanena varuṇa-ādīnām abhipraiti — the plural includes Varuṇa and other gods as well
16.translation: Kṛṣṇa resolves upon the lifting of Govardhana: ‘I shall counter this by my own power, and through it remove from the world-rulers the darkness that takes the form of pride in their divine prosperity.’ The plural indicates that the lesson extends beyond Indra to Varuṇa and other gods as well.

17.word_for_word: devāḥ sāttvikāḥ tvad-bhaktāḥ ca — objection: the gods are sāttvika and your devotees; kutaḥ teṣām tamaḥ — how then can they possess darkness; sad-bhāvaḥ sattvam mad-bhaktiḥ vā — ‘sattva’ means goodness or devotion to me; tad-yuktānām surāṇām īśā vayam iti vismayaḥ garvaḥ na ghaṭate — pride in thinking ‘we are rulers’ is incompatible with that state; ataḥ asantaḥ te — insofar as they possess such pride, they fall from genuine goodness; teṣām māna-bhaṅgaḥ anugrahaḥ eva — breaking their pride is therefore itself grace
17.translation: One might object: ‘The gods are sāttvika and devotees of yours; how can they be in darkness?’ Genuine sattva—or devotion to Kṛṣṇa—is incompatible with the proud astonishment ‘We are the rulers.’ To the extent that such pride arises, they have departed from true goodness. Therefore the breaking of their pride is not hostility but an act of grace.

19.word_for_word: kṛtvā utkṛtya — having lifted up or torn free; chattrākam — like an umbrella; ucchilīndhram — like a mushroom
19.translation: He lifted the mountain up and held it like an umbrella—Śrīdhara compares its shape to a broad mushroom.

20.word_for_word: yathopajoṣam — as each pleased; yathā-sukham — comfortably, according to convenience
20.translation: ‘Yathopajoṣam’ means that everyone should remain there comfortably, each according to convenience.

21.word_for_word: sa-vrajāḥ — together with their Vraja households and belongings; śakaṭa-maṇḍala-sahitāḥ — accompanied by the circles of carts; sa-upajīvinaḥ — together with dependents; bhṛtya-purohita-ādi-sahitāḥ — including servants, priests and others
21.translation: They entered the shelter with all of Vraja: their carts, households and all who depended upon them, including servants, priests and the rest.

23.word_for_word: padāt — from the place; sthānāt — from his position
23.translation: ‘From the foot/place’ means simply ‘from his position.’

26.word_for_word: vyuda-prāyāḥ — nearly emptied of water; vigata-udaka-prāyāḥ — with almost all water gone; svalpa-jalāḥ — containing little water
26.translation: The clouds had become nearly emptied of their water; only a little remained in them.

27.word_for_word: śakaṭa-ūḍha-upakaraṇam — equipment carried upon carts; śakaṭaiḥ ūḍham upakaraṇam — the household goods transported in the carts; yathā bhavati tathā — in that manner
27.translation: The expression means their household equipment and provisions carried upon the carts.

29.word_for_word: nibhṛtāḥ — fully satisfied, filled; yathā-yathocitam parirambhaṇa-ādibhiḥ samīyuḥ — they approached him, each appropriately, with embraces and other gestures; sad-āśiṣaḥ — excellent blessings; śreṣṭhān āśīrvādān — the best benedictions
29.translation: Their hearts full, they approached Kṛṣṇa in ways appropriate to their relationships—some embracing him and others showing affection differently—and the elders bestowed their finest blessings upon him.

33.word_for_word: tataḥ govardhana-sthānāt — then from the place of Govardhana; asya śrī-kṛṣṇasya tathā-vidhāni — such deeds of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; govardhana-uddharaṇa — especially the lifting of Govardhana
33.translation: Then they departed from the place of Govardhana, continuing to speak of Śrī Kṛṣṇa's extraordinary deeds, above all his lifting of the mountain.
